text: The core of finance is "the allocation of funds across time and space," and the main research directions include: Microfinance: Focuses on the financial decisions of individuals and enterprises, such as: How individuals can increase their wealth through savings and investments (stocks, funds, bonds, etc.); How enterprises can raise funds through equity financing (listing) and debt financing (issuing bonds and loans), and how to manage cash flow and capital structure. Macroeconomics: Focuses on the interaction between the financial system and the macroeconomy, such as: How central banks regulate the money supply through monetary policies (interest rates, reserve requirements, etc.) to stabilize prices and economic growth; The overall operation rules of financial markets (such as the stock and bond markets), as well as the impact of exchange rates and inflation on the financial system. Financial Instruments and Markets: Studies the design and trading mechanisms of various financial products, such as: Basic instruments: Stocks (ownership certificates of enterprises), bonds (creditor-debtor certificates), and foreign exchange (the exchange of different currencies); Derivative instruments: Futures (standardized contracts), options (option contracts), and swaps (agreements for interest rate or currency exchange), mainly used for hedging risks or speculation. Risk Management: Analyzes uncertainties in financial activities (such as market risk, credit risk, and liquidity risk) and reduces risks through investment diversification, financial derivatives, etc. (for example, enterprises use foreign exchange futures to hedge against losses caused by exchange rate fluctuations).
